title: Structured Backend: Structure a Backend with Routes, Controllers, Services
problem_statement:
Build a well-structured Express backend that follows the MVC (Model-View-Controller) pattern with clear separation of concerns. The application should have routes, controllers, and services organized in separate modules.

Requirements:

1. Project structure:
   - Separate the application into modules:
     - routes/ - Route definitions (URL patterns)
     - controllers/ - Request/response handling logic
     - services/ - Business logic and data operations
     - models/ - Data models/interfaces
   - Each module should have a single responsibility

2. Models:
   - Define a User model with fields: id, name, email, createdAt
   - Define a Task model with fields: id, title, completed, userId, createdAt
   - Use simple JavaScript objects or TypeScript interfaces

3. Services:
   - UserService: Methods for CRUD operations on users
   - TaskService: Methods for CRUD operations on tasks, including filtering by userId
   - Services should handle data validation and business logic
   - Services should not know about HTTP (no req/res objects)

4. Controllers:
   - UserController: Handles HTTP requests/responses for users
   - TaskController: Handles HTTP requests/responses for tasks
   - Controllers should call services and format HTTP responses
   - Controllers should handle HTTP-specific concerns (status codes, etc.)

5. Routes:
   - User routes: GET /api/users, GET /api/users/:id, POST /api/users, PUT /api/users/:id, DELETE /api/users/:id
   - Task routes: GET /api/tasks, GET /api/tasks/:id, POST /api/tasks, PUT /api/tasks/:id, DELETE /api/tasks/:id, GET /api/users/:userId/tasks
   - Routes should map to controller methods

6. Error handling:
   - Create a centralized error handling middleware
   - Create custom error classes (NotFoundError, ValidationError, etc.)
   - Services should throw custom errors
   - Controllers should not catch errors (let them propagate to error middleware)

7. Data storage:
   - Use in-memory arrays for simplicity
   - Services should manage the data storage

Use Express.js. Do not use frameworks like NestJS or Mongoose. Keep the structure simple but demonstrate clear separation of concerns.
instructions: Submit exactly one file containing the complete structured backend implementation. Separate each module using clear comments such as // === FILE: models/user.model.js ===, // === FILE: services/user.service.js ===, etc. Include all modules (models, services, controllers, routes) and the main server file. Include a brief explanation of the MVC pattern and separation of concerns. Do not submit a folder or ZIP.

rubrics.criterion: Module structure and separation of concerns
rubrics.full: Organizes the application into clear modules (models, services, controllers, routes) with proper separation of concerns. Each module has a single, well-defined responsibility.
rubrics.partial: Has some module separation but responsibilities are mixed or unclear in some modules.
rubrics.zero: Does not separate the application into modules or separation is incorrect.

rubrics.full: Services implement business logic and data operations correctly, do not handle HTTP concerns, validate data, and throw appropriate custom errors.
rubrics.partial: Services exist but have HTTP concerns, missing validation, or incorrect error handling.
rubrics.zero: Services are not implemented or do not follow service layer principles.

rubrics.full: Controllers handle HTTP requests/responses correctly, call services, format HTTP responses with appropriate status codes, and do not contain business logic.
rubrics.partial: Controllers exist but have business logic mixed in or incorrect HTTP handling.
rubrics.zero: Controllers are not implemented or do not follow controller layer principles.

rubrics.full: Routes map correctly to controller methods, all required routes are implemented, error handling is centralized with custom error classes, and errors propagate correctly.
rubrics.partial: Routes are mostly correct but have missing mappings or error handling is incomplete.
rubrics.zero: Routes are incorrect or error handling is missing.

valid_alternatives: Use TypeScript with interfaces for models if preferred.
Add additional layers (e.g., repositories) if desired.
Use different naming conventions as long as they are consistent.
Add additional features (e.g., logging middleware) if desired.
mistakes_to_check: Mixing HTTP concerns in services (Service layer violations).
Putting business logic in controllers (Controller layer violations).
Not using custom error classes or handling errors incorrectly (Error handling).
Routes not mapping to controller methods (Route configuration).
Models not defined or missing required fields (Model definitions).
Not following MVC pattern or unclear separation of concerns (Architecture).
